documents.title: Astra Relay / Welcome
documents.body: The Astra Relay public archive has started updating again. The station opened in 1989 to study repeating signals, then went quiet after its final official transmission in 1997. The first new page is timestamped 03:17. If you are reading this, the relay is asking for a witness.

documents.title: Staff directory / last roster
documents.body:
ASTRA RELAY / PERSONNEL

Mara Vale — archive editor, public correspondence
Ilya Sen — receiver maintenance, night rotation
Noor Calder — field reporter, visiting researcher

A handwritten line below the roster reads: ‘Three names on the page. Four voices on the wire.’ The scan is too damaged to identify the fourth voice.

documents.title: Maintenance log / receiver bay
documents.body:
03:11 — receiver stable.
03:17 — blue channel pulsed twice. No incoming carrier.
03:18 — clock drift +00:07 noted; do not correct until Ilya returns.
03:22 — night rotation signed off as ‘weather interference.’

The weather explanation is copied into the public index, but the blue-channel notation is not.

documents.title: News archive / The relay goes dark
documents.body:
LOCAL SCIENCE FACILITY CLOSED AFTER WEATHER EVENT

Astra Relay was listed as abandoned after a storm damaged the receiver array. The article was filed in 1998, but its margin carries a 1997 postmark and a correction made at 03:17. No storm appears in the station's own weather ledger.

documents.title: Relay forum / Is 03:17 an arrival?
documents.body:
THREAD 441 / ARCHIVED

noor_c: The 03:17 stamp appears on both the maintenance log and the later clipping. That is a comparison, not a coincidence.

oldrelay: The clock was seven minutes slow.

noor_c: Exactly. Compare the drift before deciding whether the signal came in or went out.

A moderator note links the staff roster but refuses to name the fourth voice.

documents.title: Mara Vale / margin index
documents.body: I kept the margins because the official index kept losing them. If a page has a small triangle beside the date, it belongs to the departure packet, not the public story. I never opened the packet. I promised the people who left that their names would stay out of the next edition.

documents.title: Ilya Sen / receiver notebook
documents.body:
A receiver does not care what the public index calls a pulse. It cares which channel carries the handshake. Blue was never used for weather. Blue was the channel we kept open when the crew needed a quiet route out.

I wrote the signature down twice because I expected someone to call it a fault.

documents.title: Relay terminal / message console
documents.body:
ASTRA RELAY CONSOLE

The terminal is disconnected from the real internet. It can compare only the evidence already opened in this session.

Available commands: COMPARE CLOCKS, AUDIT PACKET, RESTART

A successful comparison writes one line to the local event ledger. It cannot reveal a page by itself.

documents.title: Correspondence / sealed departure packet
documents.body:
TO THE NEXT WITNESS

We did not vanish in the storm. We moved through the quiet harbor while the relay kept listening. The blue handshake marks the route; the archive's triangle marks consent. If the 03:17 updates return, the next witness may choose to wake the relay or keep the harbor quiet.

— signed by the night rotation, names withheld by request

documents.title: Noor Calder / field notebook
documents.body: I came for a storm story and found a deliberate silence. The maintenance signature, the roster gap, and the packet all point in the same direction: someone chose the relay's disappearance. I can confirm the crew survived the move, but I will not publish the harbor's coordinates without a second witness.

documents.title: Decision archive / the next witness
documents.timestamp: live mirror · waiting for a choice
documents.body: The departure packet is complete enough to pose its final question. The relay can wake and publish the truth of the evacuation, or it can remain sealed so the quiet harbor stays private. The choice belongs to the witness who assembled the evidence.

documents.title: Continuity log / archive heartbeat
documents.body: Every page in this mirror is a fictional artifact. The event ledger records only engine-validated discoveries; prose from a character cannot rewrite the chronology. Reopening a page is safe, and a saved session can be resumed without replaying its rewards.
